content.text:
Image 1: Seven-panel storyboard reference, used for the overall shot structure, shot sizes, and camera-movement rhythm. Read it from left to right and from top to bottom; panel N is Shot N.
Image 2: Live-action reference of The Quinn family mansion, living room, used as the benchmark for environmental composition, lighting, and realistic live-action texture; it contains no people.
Image 3: Subject 1 (Lauren) character appearance reference.
Image 4: Subject 2 (George) character appearance reference.
Image 5: Subject 3 (Natalie) character appearance reference.
[Subject settings]
Subject 1 (Lauren): Refer to Image 3. 50, George's second wife and Natalie's stepmother, Cassie's mother; the controlling matriarch of the Quinn mansion. Outfit: A fitted crimson-red long-sleeve knee-length sheath dress with a round neckline, a thin gold belt at the waist, nude pointed-toe high heels and a pearl necklace. All plain, with no logos. Signature colour: red.
Subject 2 (George): Refer to Image 4. 55, Natalie's father, head of the Quinn family, remarried to Lauren. Outfit: A camel-brown fine-knit quarter-zip long-sleeve sweater over a white collared shirt. Charcoal-grey tailored wool trousers and dark-brown leather loafers. All plain, with no logos. Signature colour: brown.
Subject 3 (Natalie): Refer to Image 5. 25, George's daughter from his first marriage, struggling to pay for her sick mother's dialysis; the drama's heroine. Outfit: A worn light-blue knit cardigan, open, over a plain white crew-neck short-sleeve cotton T-shirt. Faded mid-blue straight-leg jeans and plain white canvas sneakers. She carries a simple brown canvas shoulder bag. Everything is plain, with no logos or prints. Signature colour: blue.
Environment (The Quinn family mansion, living room): Refer to Image 2. Day, soft natural daylight from the tall windows. Soft natural daylight comes through the sheer curtains of the windows on the left wall at frame left. The chandelier is unlit and faint warm wall sconces glow. Live sound is quiet room tone and a faint creak of the sofa.
Do not swap the characters' appearances, clothing, actions, positions or dialogue.
[Overall style]
Photorealistic live-action short drama with cinematic lighting. Each character keeps the face and the outfit with its main colour from their reference image throughout. Use each character sheet only for that character: the face from the close-up on the right, the body and outfit from the turnaround on the left; do not render the sheet's layout, white background or multiple views. This segment has 5 lines, in this order: Lauren, Lauren, Natalie, Cassie (V.O.), Natalie. Generate speech only from the lines in {} in the shot list, each spoken exactly once by its speaker; everyone else keeps their mouth naturally closed while listening, and a V.O. speaker keeps their mouth closed or is off screen. Follow the shot list below; do not add cuts or camera moves beyond it. Strictly adhere to the 180-degree rule: within a scene, characters keep their screen sides and the camera stays on one side of the axis. Seamless continuity of action, spatial matching and consistent actor blocking; cut on action. For dialogue prefer static shot-reverse-shot and over-the-shoulder shots, balanced with reaction shots and close-up inserts. Faces stable and clear, consistent with the reference images, with no resemblance to any real actor or actress. Normal human eyes. Natural anatomy and hands. Natural, fluid motion that follows the blocking; characters make subtle, natural movements. Characters, props and environment share one world with matched lighting. Each line ends naturally with breathing room and is never cut off. Authentic performances with micro-expressions. No BGM; generate only dialogue, environmental sounds and action sounds. No subtitles.
[Strictly exclude]
Cassie in frame. George speaking or moving his lips. hands patting, clasping, gripping or overlapping each other or an object in frame. Natalie's tears disappearing after they fall. subtitles or captions. Dialogue from the wrong character, multiple people speaking at once, repeated or missing lines, lip-sync errors and audio-visual desynchronization. The raw reference images (character sheets, setting plates) appearing as a frame of the video, and starting on a still frame of the setting reference. A fast zoom-in at the start, a fast pull-back at the end, unmotivated whip-pans, tilts, zooms and 360-degree orbits. Axis-crossing, jump cuts, frame skips, flicker and clipping. Characters or props popping in or vanishing, and duplicate characters except mirror reflections. Readable text, numbers, logos and watermarks; phones and paper are shown from the back or out of focus. Black-and-white, monochrome, grayscale, desaturated visuals; hand-drawn, sketch, line art, illustration, comics, animation; storyboard frames, rough sketches, panel borders, gutters and grid layouts.
[Shot list] (7 shots, approximately 17 seconds)
When a previous-shot reference image is given, Shot 1 matches its camera position, shot size and blocking and continues from that moment; do not repeat that frame later.
At the start: The camera stays on the near side of the coffee table, facing the back wall, windows at frame left. Natalie stands just inside the right-wall doorway at frame right, beside the empty front-right armchair, facing the sofa with pressed lips and no smile. Her eyes are glassy without tears, the flat hospital statement is at her side and her bag hangs from her shoulder. Cassie stands at the right side of the empty front-left armchair, on the coffee-table side, arms relaxed; every shot is framed to exclude her, so she stays out of frame. Lauren sits on the sofa's right end, facing camera, hands still in her lap. George sits slumped on the sofa's left end beside her, facing camera, hands still on his knees.
Shot 1 (0-2s): [Medium shot, two-shot, eye-level, locked-off, facing the back wall from just beyond the coffee table's far edge, so Cassie stands behind the camera. Framed from the seat cushions up, with the arched fireplace alcove and the framed painting behind the two of them; the right-wall doorway and Natalie lie beyond frame right. George is on frame left and Lauren on frame right, both facing camera.] Lauren turns on the sofa toward George and leans in with a cold smile, her hands still in her lap. George sits slumped, his hands on his knees. Dialogue (Lauren, in English, sweetly cold): {Natalie is also your daughter.}
Shot 2 (2-5s): [Medium close-up, eye-level, slight push in from beyond the coffee table's far edge, facing the back wall on Lauren, framed on her face and shoulders; Cassie stands behind the camera. Behind Lauren are the sofa back and the potted fig at the right of the arch. The sofa's left end lies beyond frame left and the right-wall doorway with Natalie beyond frame right.] Lauren tips her head toward frame right, toward Natalie by the right-wall doorway, and smirks with contempt. Dialogue (Lauren, in English, sneering, mocking): {She can be the one who marries Sebastard De-Klein.}
Shot 3 (5-7s): [Medium shot, eye-level, handheld from the near side facing the right wall on Natalie by the doorway. Behind her are only the pale grey right wall and the doorway frame; Cassie and the sofa lie beyond frame left.] Natalie shakes her head and takes a half step back toward the right-wall doorway, her eyes glassy, no smile. Her hands hang apart at her sides below frame. Dialogue (Natalie, in English, firm but shaky): {No, I'm not going to.}
Shot 4 (7-11s): [Close-up, high angle from the near side facing the right wall on Natalie's face, slow tilt down from her eyes to her trembling lips. Behind her are only the pale grey right wall and the marble floor. Her hands and the statement stay out of frame.] Natalie looks down toward the hospital statement at her side. Her eyes fill with tears that spill down her cheeks, and her mouth stays closed. Cassie is off screen. Dialogue (Cassie, V.O., in English, sing-song, taunting): {Do you want us to pay for your mother's medical bills or not?}
Shot 5 (11-13s): [Medium shot, high angle from the near side on George at the sofa's left end, locked-off, framed on his chest and face. Behind him are only the sofa cushion and the ivory rug. The sofa's right end, with Lauren, lies beyond frame right.] George keeps his lips pressed shut, turns his eyes away from Natalie and stares at the ivory rug, his hands still on his knees.
Shot 6 (13-15s): [Medium shot, low angle from beyond the coffee table's far edge, facing the back wall on Lauren at the sofa's right end, framed on her from the knees up; Cassie stands behind the camera. Behind her are the upper back wall and the potted fig at the right of the arch. The frame is tight at frame left so the sofa's left end lies beyond it, and tight at frame right at the fig so the right-wall doorway and Natalie lie beyond frame right.] Lauren crosses her legs, leans back and lifts her chin expectantly toward Natalie beyond frame right, her hands resting still in her lap.
Shot 7 (15-17s): [Close-up, eye-level, locked-off from the near side facing the right wall on Natalie's face. Behind her is only the pale grey right wall beside the doorway frame.] Natalie closes her wet eyes and exhales, her shoulders dropping, tear streaks still shining on her cheeks. Dialogue (Natalie, in English, quiet, defeated): {Fine.}
At the end: The camera stays on the near side of the coffee table, facing the back wall, windows at frame left. Natalie stands just inside the right-wall doorway at frame right, beside the empty front-right armchair. Her eyes are closed and wet, with tear-streaked cheeks; the flat hospital statement is at her side and her bag hangs from her shoulder. Cassie stands at the right side of the empty front-left armchair, on the coffee-table side, out of frame. Lauren sits back on the sofa's right end with her legs crossed and her hands still in her lap. George sits on the sofa's left end, staring at the rug, hands still on his knees.
